major_concerns: Vendor grammar completeness and provenance (incomplete grammars could bias results).
Emulator fidelity vs real device semantics may misestimate semantic error rates.
Validation ground truth for semantic failures may be ambiguous without a proven oracle.
Tokenization/decoder integration across vendors may introduce engineering artefacts.
required_design_repairs: Specify precise sources and coverage tests for each vendor grammar; publish grammar artifacts.
Include a validated semantic-oracle (or gold-config set) for a subset of intents to estimate validator false-negatives/positives.
Define tokenization and decoder-integration tests to rule out engineering-induced parse errors.
Predefine emulator-to-device semantic-mismatch checks and sensitivity analyses (e.g., cross-validate on a limited set of physical device logs if available).

major_concerns: Simulated human-in-the-loop policy may not reflect operator behavior and will bias arm B comparisons.
Automated repairs may introduce regressions that are hard to attribute without per-iteration logging.
Validator coverage and formal specification must be frozen and justified; gaps will invalidate conclusions.
Risk of iterative model calls producing degenerate/overfit repair behaviors if not constrained.
required_design_repairs: Preregister and publish the simulated HITL decision policy and justify it; include sensitivity analysis to alternate policies.
Define and freeze validator formal specification, error-code taxonomy, and unit tests before execution.
Limit and preregister maximum repair attempts, stopping rules, and randomness control; instrument per-iteration diffs and causal logs.
Include metrics for repair-induced regressions and a procedure to adjudicate ambiguous repair outcomes (e.g., oracle subset).

major_concerns: Realism of injected telemetry noise, visibility masks, and legacy behavior models is subjective and may drive results.
Failure-labeling for semantically subtle errors may be subjective without annotation protocol and inter-annotator checks.
Choice of intents/topologies could dominate transfer estimates if not sufficiently diverse.
required_design_repairs: Formalize noise and legacy-model definitions with references and parameter ranges; publish generators.
Establish labeling protocol with blinded annotators, inter-annotator agreement targets, and adjudication rules; preregister annotator counts.
Ensure a pre-specified diverse topology and vendor stratification; if possible, include multiple independent intent corpora and sensitivity analyses.
Preregister concordance metrics and bootstrap procedures used for inference.

major_concerns: Ethical and dual-use risk from publishing attack payloads or exploit patterns.
Simulated adversary models may not capture real attacker creativity or scale.
Mitigations' operational cost (false positives, blocked benign ops) must be measured and reported.
Scaling and integration assumptions for mitigations may not hold in real retrieval/tool ecosystems.
required_design_repairs: Add an explicit ethical-safety plan: keep all attack payloads and experiments confined to closed emulation; redact actionable payloads in public artifacts; include safe-disclosure notes.
Preregister adversary models and justify their threat realism; include a range of adversary strengths.
Define and preregister mitigation cost metrics (false-block rate, human-review workload proxies) and thresholds for acceptable operational impact.
Include ablation and scalability analyses for mitigations and instrument provenance/forensics signals for reproducibility.
